html:
The Viceroyalty of New Granada was the Spanish government of northern South America, covering today's Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador and Panama, with its capital at Santa Fe de Bogotá. Spain carved it out of the Viceroyalty of Peru in 1717, suspended it in 1723 to save money, and restored it for good in 1739. It was part of Spanish America.

Its key city was the fortified Caribbean port of Cartagena, which held off a huge British attack in 1741. Gold from its rivers was the main export. New taxes under the Bourbon reforms set off the Revolt of the Comuneros in 1781.

In 1810 local juntas took power in Bogotá and Caracas. Spain fought back, but Simón Bolívar won at the Battle of Boyacá in 1819, and the old viceroyalty became the republic of Gran Colombia. That broke up in 1830 into Colombia, Venezuela and Ecuador.
